checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add an append-only anchor journal (assay transfer) so each run's head commits to the previous anchor

impact_assessment.why: Cycle 58 added a single mutable .anchor sidecar; deleting or rewinding it is detectable only if an external copy exists. assay/anchor.py:210 AnchorJournal chains each anchor to the previous anchor hash, so a rolled-back or deleted anchor is detectable.
impact_assessment.benefits: Two or more run heads form a verified journal; verify_chain(journal_path=...) detects a truncated log against the latest anchor; tampered/deleted anchors are named by prev/hash findings; the single .anchor API stays compatible.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new .anchors JSONL sidecar and verify_chain keyword; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: append under the existing telemetry lock discipline; state: sidecar only, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the single anchor unchanged; validate schema/head/seq/prev/hash on read; append atomically with fsync; test intact, truncated, deleted-anchor, backwards-seq and legacy single-anchor paths; full 179-test and AIKit gates.

[1/4] Plan: optional HMAC-SHA256 telemetry records (assay record_mac pattern)

impact_assessment.why: Brain's chain is unkeyed: an attacker who recomputes every digest and prev can rewrite the log undetected. assay/ledger.py:29 record_mac signs the canonical payload with a verifier-held key.
impact_assessment.benefits: Telemetry(path, hmac_key=...) writes a mac per record; verify_chain(hmac_key=...) reports missing-mac/bad-mac; unkeyed logs and bytes remain unchanged; wrong keys and tampered payloads are named.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: optional mac field and constructor/verifier keyword; dependency: stdlib hmac only; concurrency: MAC computed under the existing append lock; state: key material stays outside the repo.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep hmac_key optional and bytes-only; exclude mac from the digest; compute mac over the canonical record including digest; test correct/wrong/missing/tampered keys and unkeyed parity; full 186-test and AIKit gates.

[1/4] Plan: token-budgeted model prompts via research-engine estimate_tokens/pack

impact_assessment.why: Brain's prompt builder has no token cap; a long observation (target/items/obstacles/visits) can grow without bound and is not auditable against a context budget. research-engine/engine/context.py:35,45 provides a stable 4-chars/token estimate and a first-line-preserving pack.
impact_assessment.benefits: Optional max_tokens keeps the base + essential extras and drops trailing visits/optional lines; prompt_stats reports tokens/omitted/lines; LlamaCppBackend(prompt_budget=...) applies it; default None keeps the existing prompt byte-identical.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: build_prompt gains max_tokens and prompt_stats, LlamaCppBackend gains prompt_budget; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the first line as the anchor; put visits last so it is dropped first; default None preserves all current prompts; test exact uncapped text, budgeted tokens/omitted, essential fields, fake-server prompt cap, and existing batteries.

[1/4] Plan: Merkle batch anchors and inclusion proofs (merklock hashing transfer)

impact_assessment.why: The linear hash chain and anchor journal prove order and continuity, but not membership of a specific record in a batch without replaying the chain. merklock/hashing.py:38-104 provides domain-separated Merkle roots, proofs and verification with odd-node promotion.
impact_assessment.benefits: A .merkle sidecar commits a contiguous batch (start/end/root); a single record gets an O(log n) inclusion proof; a truncated log, changed digest or edited root is named; no change to the log format or rule behavior.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new telemetry/merkle.py and Telemetry.write_merkle_anchor; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: atomic sidecar write; state: sidecar only, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep leaves as existing record digests, domain-separate leaf/node hashes, validate anchor ranges and detached proofs, test odd/empty trees and tamper cases, and re-run the 200-test and AIKit gates.
